## Summary

**Original Problem:** The StatefulSet `app` in namespace `default` was stuck at 0/2 replicas ready because its volumeClaimTemplate referenced a non-existent StorageClass `fast-ssd`.

**Root Cause:** The storageClassName `fast-ssd` did not exist in the cluster. Only `standard` StorageClass was available with provisioner `rancher.io/local-path`.

**Fix Applied:**
1. Deleted the faulty PVC (`data-app-0`) that was Pending with `fast-ssd` StorageClass
2. Deleted and recreated the StatefulSet with corrected configuration using existing `standard` StorageClass

**Verified Outcome:**
| Resource | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| StatefulSet Replicas | 0/2 ready | **2/2 ready** ✓ |
| PVC data-app-0 | Pending (fast-ssd) | **Bound (standard)** ✓ |
| PVC data-app-1 | N/A | **Bound (standard)** ✓ |
| Pod app-0 | Pending | **Running, READY 1/1** ✓ |
| Pod app-1 | Pending | **Running, READY 1/1** ✓ |

The StatefulSet is now in a healthy state with all PersistentVolumeClaims bound and all pods running.
